92-235.r: Bengal Partition decided (20 July 1905) → Swadeshi formally declared (7 Aug 1905, Calcutta Town Hall) → Swaraj accepted as Congress goal (Calcutta Session, Dadabhai Naoroji) → Surat Split.

92-236.r: Assertion false: Nehru respected the Upanishads and had great faith in them. Reason true: he had a scientific outlook ('father of science in modern India').

92-237.r: 'Imperialism is dead as dodo' → Clement Attlee, British Prime Minister after World War II.
92-237.h: Dodo is an extinct bird; Attlee's Britain was letting the Empire go.

92-238.r: 'Here is a revolution taking place and we should move quickly' → Sir Stafford Cripps (head of Cripps Mission 1942; member of Cabinet Mission 1946).

92-239.r: Government of India run 'with the assent and often to the dictates of the Chamber of Commerce' = 'White Man's Burden' → said by Sachchidananda Sinha.

92-240.r: First atomic bomb → Hiroshima, Japan (06 Aug 1945); second → Nagasaki (09 Aug 1945); Japan then surrendered in Aug 1945.

92-241.r: French Revolution began → 1789; middle-class revolt against feudalism, class privilege, autocracy and incompetent monarchy.

92-242.r: Champaran (1917, Bihar) → Amritsar case / Jallianwala Bagh (13 April 1919) → Moplah Revolt (1921, Kerala) → Chauri-Chaura (4 Feb 1922, Gorakhpur).

92-243.r: True: Nehru died (1964) in his 4th term as PM; first non-Congress PM took office in 1977. False: Nehru represented Phulpur (near Prayagraj), not Rae Bareli.

92-244.r: Lucknow Pact (1916) → Gandhi-Irwin Pact (5 March 1931) → Poona Pact (1932) → final withdrawal of Civil Disobedience Movement.

92-245.r: Lucknow Pact → 1916 (Dec, joint session); Gandhi-Irwin Pact → 1931, not 1932; Desai-Liaquat Pact → 1945; Shimla → 1945, not 1946; Poona → 1932, not 1947.
92-245.c: No answer printed; by the explanation both (a) Lucknow 1916 and (c) Desai-Liaquat 1945 look correct.

92-246.r: Wrong pair: Suresh Tendulkar → economist, not political scientist. Correct: Fateh Singh Rathore → Tiger Man; Mani Kanal → film maker; R.S. Sharma → historian.

92-247.r: Bardoli → Gujarat; Chauri-Chaura → Uttar Pradesh (Gorakhpur); Yerwada Jail → Maharashtra; Noakhali (riots at independence) → now in Bangladesh.
92-247.c: No answer printed: Noakhali is in Bangladesh, not West Bengal; apart from that, code (c) fits.

92-248.r: Wrong: Vande Mataram 'originally in Bengali' — Bankim used Bengali and Sanskrit (in Anand Math). True: Flag design adopted 22 July 1947; Jana-Gana-Mana adopted 24 Jan 1950.

92-249.r: Khrushchev-Bulganin visit India (after Nehru's USSR visit, 1955) → Dalai Lama flees to India (1959) → Chou-en-Lai visits Delhi (April 1960) → Goa liberated (1961).

92-250.r: Shimla Agreement → 1972 (June-July), Indira Gandhi and Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto, after the 1971 war and Bangladesh's independence.

92-251.r: Operation Vijay (1999) → successful Indian military action against Pakistan.

92-252.r: Kisan Diwas → 23 December, in remembrance of ex-Prime Minister Chaudhary Charan Singh.

92-253.r: Rabindranath Tagore → Literature (Nobel 1913, Gitanjali; first Indian Nobel winner); Amartya Sen → Economics (1998); Chandrasekhar → Astrophysics (Physics Nobel 1983); Vinoo Mankad → Cricket.

92-255.r: Chandra Shekhar Azad martyred (27 Feb 1931) → Gandhi-Irwin Pact (5 March 1931) → Bhagat Singh executed (23 March 1931) → Karachi Session (29-31 March 1931).
92-255.h: All four fall within about five weeks of early 1931: Azad, Pact, Execution, Karachi.

92-256.r: Lahore Session (Dec 1929) → Gandhi-Irwin Pact (5 March 1931) → Rajguru, Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev executed (23 March 1931) → Karachi Session (29-31 March 1931).

92-257.r: Subhash Chandra Bose → Haripura Session (INC); Vallabhbhai Patel → Operation Polo; Iqbal → Allahabad Session of Muslim League 1930; Batukeshwar Dutt → bomb in Central Assembly.

92-258.r: Butler Committee (1927, Sir Harcourt Butler) → define relationship between Government of India (Paramount Power) and Indian States; visited 16 states, reported 1929.

92-259.r: Privy purses and special rights of former princely rulers abolished → 26th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1971.

92-260.r: First All India Socialist Youth Congress → Calcutta, 27 Dec 1928, presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru.

92-261.r: Hind Mazdoor Sabha (Calcutta, Dec 1948) → founders Ashok Mehta, T.S. Ramanujam, G.G. Mehta; first President R.S. Ruikar, General Secretary Ashok Mehta.

92-262.r: Alipore Central Jail → Kolkata (established 1906); held political prisoners under British rule.

92-263.r: Operation Polo (Sept 1948) → Indian military action in Hyderabad State; Nizam overthrown and state annexed to Indian Union.
92-263.t: Don't confuse Hyderabad (Operation Polo) with Junagarh, the other option.

92-264.r: Writers' Building → Secretariat of West Bengal, Kolkata; designed by Thomas Lyon, built 1777 for East India Company's junior servants ('Writers').

92-265.r: Teen Murti Bhavan (Nehru's residence) → converted into Prime Ministers Museum, inaugurated by PM Narendra Modi on 14 April 2022.

92-266.r: Karl Marx explained class struggle through dialectical materialism ('materialistic interpretation of history': history shaped by economic causes).

92-267.r: False: 'not an Indian citizen at death' — Mother Teresa was an Indian citizen when she died (5 Sept 1997). True: joined a mission at 18; taught in Calcutta (St. Mary's).

92-268.r: Mother Teresa's religious organisation → Missionaries of Charity.
92-268.t: Not 'Sisters of Charity'; the correct name is Missionaries of Charity.

92-269.r: China and Tibet → book answer 1959 (Tibetan uprising crushed, Dalai Lama fled, autonomy ended); China's invasion and control of Tibet began about nine years earlier.
92-269.c: Partly wrong: China invaded and took control of Tibet about nine years earlier; 1959 is when the Tibetan uprising was crushed, the Dalai Lama fled and Tibet's autonomy ended. Of these options, 1959 fits best.

92-270.r: USSR broke up into fifteen countries including Russia → 26 Dec 1991.

92-271.r: Bangladesh became independent after Indo-Pak war of Dec 1971; freedom movement began 26 March 1971; East Pakistan became Bangladesh on 16 Dec 1971.

92-272.r: German unification (East and West Germany reunited) → 3 October 1990.

92-273.r: USA joined World War II militarily after Japan attacked Pearl Harbour (7 Dec 1941); war began 1 Sept 1939 with Germany's invasion of Poland.

92-275.r: Richard Nixon (37th US President) → only US President to resign, over the Watergate Scandal.

92-276.r: Bishop Desmond Tutu → South Africa; anti-racism leader; Nobel Peace Prize 1984, Gandhi Peace Prize 2005.

92-277.r: Real paper first made in China → Tsai-Lun (105 A.D.).

92-278.r: Plato was a disciple of Socrates; Aristotle was a disciple of Plato. Plato's 'The Republic' discusses justice and the 'Ideal State'.
92-278.h: S-P-A, teacher to pupil: Socrates → Plato → Aristotle.

92-279.r: Main cause of the Italian Renaissance (14th century, start of modern era) → freedom to express ideas.

92-280.r: Kallar → South Indian tribe that revolted against the British; belonged to Madurai region.

92-281.r: Act of 1909 → introduced separate electorate for Muslims.

92-282.r: Rama Devi → woman revolutionary arrested in Bijoliya Peasant Movement; also joined 1930 Satyagraha and 1932 Civil Disobedience and was jailed.
92-282.c: The explanation describes a different woman, Rama Devi Choudhury of Odisha ('Maa'); the Rama Devi meant here was a Rajasthan activist of the Bijoliya peasant movement.

92-283.r: Indian National Congress → 1885; Bhartiya Jan Sangh → 1951; Communist Party of India → 1925; A.I.A.D.M.K. → 1972.

92-284.r: 'Imperial Gazetteer of India' → compiled by William Wilson Hunter (Indian Civil Service).

92-285.r: Name 'Panchayati Raj' for rural local government → suggested by Mahatma Gandhi (villages economically, politically and administratively independent).

92-286.r: Indian National Calendar: first month Chaitra (March-April); last month Phalgun.

93-001.r: Raja Rammohan Roy's 'Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhiddin' (Gift to Monotheists, 1809) → written in Persian; English translation by Maulavi Obaidullah, 1884.
93-001.c: No answer printed; UKPSC cancelled the question. Explanation says Persian.

93-003.r: Annie Besant → 'New India' and 'The Commonweal' (1914). Hind Swaraj → Mahatma Gandhi; India Wins Freedom → Abul Kalam Azad.
93-003.t: The Commonweal was Annie Besant's paper, not Tilak's.

93-005.r: 'India Wins Freedom' → autobiography of Maulana Abul Kalam Azad.

93-006.r: 'Gita Rahasya' (Srimad Bhagavad Gita Rahasya) → Bal Gangadhar Tilak, written in Mandalay jail.

93-008.r: 'Srimad Bhagavad Gita Rahasya' → Lokmanya Tilak's commentary on the Bhagavad Gita, in Marathi.

93-009.r: Aurobindo Ghosh → 'The Life Divine', 'The Ideal of Human Unity'; attacked Bengal Partition in his paper 'Vande Mataram'; jailed 1908; settled in Pondicherry 1910.

93-010.r: Col. James Tod → first to write on 'Feudalism' in Rajasthan (19th century), in 'Annals and Antiquities of Rajasthan'.

93-011.r: Vital-Vidhvansak (1888, Marathi) → first monthly journal aimed at untouchables, published by Gopal Baba Walangkar.
